title: Return every drive to the bay it came from
instruction: Put each drive back into the bay it came from; the storage array only rebuilds if every drive is in its own bay.
context: Data-centre storage service: identical drive sleds pulled for a chassis swap must go back into their original bays or the array will not rebuild. Nothing on a sled says which bay it came from.
setup: On a wooden bench in front of two arms mounted 61 cm apart: a grey storage enclosure (14 x 20 cm base, fixed) 27 cm in front of the arm bases on the centre line with three top-loading bays (slots 12.5 x 4 cm, 2.5 cm deep, 6 mm walls, running away from the arms) at 6 cm left, centre, and 6 cm right; three identical black drive sleds (10 x 2 x 7 cm, 150 g) standing in the bays at reset; a dark service cart (fixed) 13 cm out with four slots of the same kind, 2.5 cm deep, at 6 cm and 12 cm left and right of the centre line. During the first 6.8 s, while the arms are held still, the operator lifts the sleds out one at a time (at 1, 3 and 5 s, 1.4 s each) and stands each in a cart slot; the order and the slot choice change between trials (cycles through all 24 arrangements). The robot is commanded from 6.8 s.
scoring: 1/3 per sled standing in the bay it came from (centre within 1 cm across the slot and 2 cm along it, bottom within 1 cm of the bay floor, tilt under 10 degrees, still); success (1.0) when all three hold for 1 s. The episode ends with the score so far if a sled is set down in another bay or dropped off the bench.
run_limit: 1200 steps (60 seconds at 20 Hz), including the 6.8 s observation phase during which actions are ignored
reset_notes: Stand the three sleds in the bays; pick the next arrangement and move them to the cart slots as described.
fidelity: Approximate: sleds are rigid blocks; bays and cart slots are rail pockets with 7 mm side clearance.
